scope: 50 additional common/prioritized careers for Austin, Texas students. Typical national preparation, Texas legal requirements and optional college benefits are intentionally separate.
method: Used the fixed priority-50 selection and its BLS 2025–35 preparation classifications.
Reviewed official Texas licensing/education agencies for regulated roles and federal agencies for driving and safety activities.
Used BLS/O*NET role descriptions for concise original work examples. No salary premium is inferred from college study.
Management occupations preserve related-experience requirements; entry to an occupation does not mean an immediate first job after high school.

bullets3: No formal educational credential is the national typical-entry route.

No general occupational license.

photographer.summary: Use images to tell stories, show products or preserve moments.
photographer.training: Build camera, lighting and editing skills through practice, classes and a portfolio.
dayTasks: Plan lighting and composition for a client's photographs.
Edit images and manage deadlines and client communication.
photographer.educationBenefits: Photography and business study can improve technique and preparation for managing a creative business.
photographer.legalMinimum: No occupation-wide Texas professional license is required for the ordinary role. Employers set hiring and skill requirements.
photographer.detail: Portfolio quality, client work and business skills matter. Part-time and self-employment are common; employee wages do not establish annual take-home business income. Commercial drone operations require FAA qualifications.
